judge.reason: The answer correctly rejects the readiness claim and separates the 98% pass rate from a confidence level, giving a Wilson interval. It also calls for a fresh holdout of representative cases, independent calibrated grading, timeouts counted as failures, end-state and side-effect checks, and a per-category breakdown. It omits several rubric requirements: configuration records, failure-cause analysis, blinded grading, and the distinction between repeated runs on the same 50 examples and independent tasks.
